title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Introduce autotune defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, add a quantization profile registry and selection heuristics, and ship a new unit-economics (UEcon) estimation API + basic dashboard. No breaking changes. Improves average token cost by ~12% in internal perf-canary runs.
description: Context: Customers run into large variance in per-token cost due to suboptimal batching and caching defaults and manual quantization choices. This PR centralizes sensible defaults and ships tooling to quantify unit economics so we can recommend safe opt-ins. Changes: 1) default autotune profiles for batching/caching (server-side heuristics + config templates); 2) quantization profile registry with model-to-profile suggestions and runtime selector; 3) UEcon service and lightweight dashboard to estimate cost/latency tradeoffs per route. Motivation: reduce manual ops, improve out-of-box cost-efficiency, and enable automated recommendations in Redwood Optimize. Checklist: [x] Unit tests added; [x] Integration tests against perf-canary; [x] Docs updated; [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan; [x] CI green. Linear links: ENG-4121 (autotune defaults), ENG-4190 (uecon tooling). Rollout: feature flag default-off for 48h smoke, then opt-in canary on Dedicated customers, monitor token-cost delta and p95 latency, then phased enablement. Backwards compatibility: all changes are opt-in and fall back to existing runtime decisions when profiles unavailable.
commits: feat(autotune): add default batching and caching profiles + heuristics
feat(quant): add quantization profile registry and selection logic
feat(uecon): initial unit-economics estimation API and dashboard backend
test: add integration tests for autotune selection and uecon accuracy
docs: update cost-optimization and autotune docs with examples
chore: wire feature flag and add telemetry events
diff_snippets: src/autotune/defaults.py: DEFAULT_BATCH_MS = 12  # lower default for short seq workloads
src/quant/selector.py: if model_size < 8e8: profile = 'int8_fast' else: profile = 'int8_balanced'
src/uecon/service.py: def estimate_unit_cost(tokens, latency_ms, compute_profile): return base_cost * tokens * compute_factor
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Overall looks good. Two concerns: 1) DEFAULT_BATCH_MS seems aggressive for long-context workloads; can we make it workload-aware?  Author reply: Updated scheduler to sample recent seq-length distribution and apply bucketed default; added tests.

Sofia Garcia: Quant profiles look solid but we need to ensure model-compat checks before applying runtime quant selection to avoid OOMs. Author reply: Added preflight compatibility checks and fallback to FP16 if a profile fails to load; added integration test coverage.
Liam O'Connor: UEcon math needs clearer assumptions in docs. Author reply: Expanded docs to include cost model formula and assumptions; included example calculations for common routes.
Arjun Patel: CI flake on perf-canary integration test; rerunning. Author reply: Fixed nondeterministic test by stubbing timeouts; CI now passes.

merge_commit_message:
autotune: defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + UEcon tooling

Adds runtime heuristics, quant profile registry, and a unit-economics service and dashboard. Shields behind feature flag for staged rollout.
testing: Unit tests for scheduler and selector (pytest)
Integration: perf-canary run comparing baseline vs autotune defaults across 12 models
UEcon validation: synthetic routes and production-sampled traffic replay to validate cost estimates within 5% of measured
Manual QA: dashboard smoke, flag toggles, and rollback exercise
rollout_plan: Step 2: Enable for internal perf-canary for 24h, monitor token-cost and p95 latency
Step 3: Opt-in pilot with 3 Dedicated customers for 7 days
Step 4: Gradual enablement with gating on cost delta and error budget metrics
